walkthroughs.body_html:
Materials & Applications — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Materials & Applications brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Materials & Applications.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What property do shape memory alloys have?
options: They return to a pre-set shape when heated.
They glow when touched.
Ductility is for metals, malleability is for plastics.
They remember every shape they have ever been bent into.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between ductility and malleability?
options: They mean exactly the same thing.
They glow when touched.
Ductility is being drawn into wires; malleability is being hammered into sheets.
Ductility is for metals, malleability is for plastics.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CAD and CAM?
options: They are the same thing with different names.
CAD creates digital designs; CAM uses those designs to control manufacturing machines.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
Ductility is for metals, malleability is for plastics.
